outputs.L1: Disclosed herein are a method and system for determining an overall value rating or value estimate for a product to be offered for sale or lease. The method includes identifying a product type associated with the product and determining a set of attributes corresponding to the identified product type. The method further includes calculating a value-score unit size for the product based on statistical data relating to the product and the product type; determining an attribute-value multiplier associated with each attribute in the set; and presenting, to a seller associated with the product, an attribute template (130) that includes the set of attributes. The method receives data from the seller relating to each attribute in the set (140). For each attribute in the attribute template, the method determines an attribute-rating value based on the received data and the attribute-value multiplier associated with that attribute (150). The method then determines the overall rating value (160) based on the sum of the attribute-rating values and an asking price submitted by the seller.
outputs.L2:
A method and system are described for generating an overall value rating or estimated value for a product intended to be sold or leased. The method first identifies the product’s type and establishes a collection of attributes applicable to that type. Using statistical information concerning both the product and its type, the method computes a value-score unit size. It also assigns an attribute-value multiplier to each attribute in the collection.

An attribute template (130), containing the identified attributes, is then provided to the seller of the product. The method obtains seller-supplied information relating to every attribute in the template (140). For each attribute, an attribute rating value is calculated from the submitted information and the corresponding attribute-value multiplier (150). Finally, the method determines the overall rating value (160) using the total of the individual attribute rating values together with the seller’s stated asking price.

The method begins by identifying the product type and determining the set of attributes relevant to that category. Using statistical data associated with both the specific product and its type, the method then calculates a value-score unit size that serves as a standardized basis for evaluation.

Next, an attribute value multiplier is assigned to each identified attribute, reflecting its relative importance to the product’s value. An attribute template containing these attributes is then presented to the seller. The seller supplies the requested data for each attribute, and the method combines each submitted value with its corresponding multiplier to calculate an individual attribute rating value.

Finally, the individual attribute rating values are summed and evaluated in relation to the seller’s asking price. This calculation produces an overall value rating, enabling the product’s value to be assessed consistently based on its characteristics, relevant market data, and listed price.
outputs.L4:
A method and system are provided for estimating and evaluating the value of a product offered for sale or lease. The system first identifies the type or category of the product and determines the attributes that are relevant to its value. Depending on the product, these attributes may include age, condition, size, features, location, performance, quality, availability, or other characteristics that affect market value.

For each product type, the system establishes statistical value units based on available market information, historical transaction data, comparable products, expert assessments, or other relevant data sources. Attribute multipliers are then calculated or assigned to reflect the relative effect of each attribute on the product’s value. The multipliers may increase or decrease the estimated value depending on whether a particular attribute is superior, inferior, or comparable to an established standard or market benchmark.

A seller provides product-specific information through a template associated with the identified product type. The template presents fields, questions, or selectable options corresponding to the relevant attributes, thereby promoting consistent data collection across similar products. The system may validate the information, identify missing or inconsistent entries, and convert the seller’s responses into numerical attribute ratings.

The individual attribute ratings are weighted using the applicable statistical value units and attribute multipliers. The weighted ratings are then combined to generate an aggregate assessment of the product’s characteristics. The system compares or integrates this assessment with the seller’s asking sale price or lease price to calculate an overall value rating. That rating indicates whether the asking price represents relatively favorable, average, or unfavorable value in view of the product’s attributes and applicable market information.

The resulting value rating may be displayed to sellers, prospective buyers or lessees, marketplace operators, or other authorized users. It may also be used to rank listings, identify comparable products, recommend a price range, or support negotiations and purchasing decisions. By applying standardized templates, statistical value units, and attribute-specific multipliers, the method provides a consistent and repeatable framework for assessing the value of different products offered for sale or lease.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract describing a method and system for calculating an overall value rating for a product offered for sale or lease based on product attributes, statistical data, seller input, and asking price.
counterfactuals.output: A computer-implemented method and system are disclosed for calculating an overall value rating for a product offered for sale or lease. Product data identifying a subject product, including one or more product attributes, seller-supplied information, and an asking price, are received by a computing device. Statistical data associated with comparable products are obtained from one or more data sources and processed to determine reference values, attribute adjustments, market trends, and expected pricing for the subject product. The product attributes and seller-supplied information may be validated, normalized, and assigned respective weights based on their relevance, reliability, or statistical correlation with transaction value. A valuation engine compares the asking price with an estimated market value generated from the statistical data and weighted attributes and calculates one or more component scores representing price competitiveness, product condition, feature desirability, seller-related factors, and market conditions. The component scores are combined to produce an overall value rating. The rating may be expressed numerically, categorically, or graphically and presented through a user interface together with supporting comparisons or recommendations. The system may update the rating in response to changes in the asking price, product information, or market data.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a technical summary of an invention that identifies a product type, generates an attribute template, assigns multipliers to attributes, collects product information from a seller, and computes a value estimate.
counterfactuals.output:
### Technical Summary

The invention relates to a computer-implemented system and method for estimating the value of a product based on product-specific attributes. The system receives information identifying a product and determines a corresponding product type, such as an electronic device, vehicle, collectible, appliance, or other category of goods.

Based on the identified product type, the system generates or retrieves an attribute template defining characteristics relevant to valuation of that product type. The attributes may include, for example, brand, model, age, condition, configuration, functionality, included accessories, provenance, usage, and geographic location. Each attribute or possible attribute value is assigned a multiplier representing its relative positive or negative effect on product value. The multipliers may be predetermined, derived from historical transaction data, generated by a statistical or machine-learning model, or adjusted according to current market conditions.

The system presents the attribute template to a seller through a user interface and collects product information supplied by the seller. The collected information may be validated, normalized, supplemented from external data sources, or verified using photographs, serial numbers, documentation, or other evidence.

A valuation engine determines a baseline value for the identified product type and applies the applicable attribute multipliers to the baseline value. In one implementation, the estimated value is calculated as:

\[
V = B \times \prod_{i=1}^{n} M_i
\]

where \(V\) is the estimated product value, \(B\) is the baseline value, and \(M_i\) is the multiplier associated with the seller-provided value of attribute \(i\). Alternative implementations may use additive adjustments, weighted scoring, regression, probabilistic modeling, or combinations thereof.

The system outputs a value estimate, optionally as a point value, value range, confidence score, or recommended listing or purchase price. The estimate may be updated dynamically as additional product information is received or as market data and attribute multipliers change. The invention thereby provides a scalable valuation framework in which product-specific templates and weighted attribute effects enable consistent estimates across different categories of products.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an abstract for a patent application covering an automated product valuation process, including value score unit sizing, attribute value multipliers, seller-completed templates, and calculation of an overall rating.
counterfactuals.output: An automated product valuation system receives product information through a seller-completed template containing predefined product attributes and corresponding attribute data. A processor determines a value score unit size based on a valuation range, scoring scale, product category, market data, or combinations thereof. Attribute value multipliers are assigned to respective product attributes according to their relative effects on product value. The processor converts the attribute data into attribute scores using the value score unit size and applies the corresponding attribute value multipliers to generate weighted attribute scores. The weighted attribute scores are aggregated and optionally adjusted using condition, demand, location, timing, confidence, or comparable-product data to calculate an overall rating for the product. The system may use the overall rating to produce an estimated value, valuation range, ranking, or recommendation and may update the template, unit size, or multipliers in response to subsequently received transaction or market data.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
